qs.q: A 6-day-old infant post-repair of oesophageal atresia is scheduled to have a diagnostic imaging study performed to check for surgical complications before starting oral feeds. Which study is indicated?
qs.e: A water-soluble contrast swallow is performed at about day 5 to 10 to look for a leak before starting oral feeds. Barium is avoided due to the risk of severe mediastinitis if a leak is present.
qs.s: Oesophageal Atresia and Tracheo-oesophageal Fistula: MCQs

qs.q: A 7-year-old child undergoes resection of a Meckel's diverticulum and develops an early postoperative complication related to the intestinal anastomosis. Which specific surgical complication should the team monitor for?
qs.e: Complications of surgery for Meckel's diverticulum include anastomotic leak, wound infection, and adhesive obstruction. Ectopic mucosal hypertrophy is not a standard postoperative anastomotic complication.
